transcript:
Header: 2025-04-03 14:00 UTC | Duration 45m | Meeting ID FF-20250403-7942
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood CSM); Dr. Elena Ruiz (MedSys Head of Data Science), Marcus Chen (CTO), Lydia Park (ML Engineer)
Shared: POC scope deck (link: redwood.io/scope/DEAL-48291), benchmark spreadsheet (link: redwood.io/bench/48291), security brief (redwood.io/sec)

Summary: Short scoping call to align on success criteria, workload sizing for the POC, and to agree a quality evaluation plan (golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination and format checks, scoring approach). Agreed next steps: exchange sample queries, Samir to share benchmark template, and schedule infra deep-dive.

Topics: POC success criteria; throughput & latency targets; dataset / golden prompts; scoring and pass/fail thresholds; hallucination detection; format/structure checks; timelines; infra and security constraints.

Transcript:
00:00 Samir Patel: okay hey everyone thanks for joining, um we're gonna kick off, um this POC scoping session for MedSys, uh goal is to nail success criteria and the quality eval plan, and then outline benchmarks and timelines.
00:12 Dr. Elena Ruiz: great thanks Samir, yeah from our side quick context we are evaluating Redwood to replace an internal inference pipeline that currently hits higher latencies and costs. We're particularly sensitive to hallucination on clinical notes and preserving structured outputs for downstream billing parsers.
00:28 Samir Patel: got it, that makes sense. Jordan, do you wanna run through the typical POC structure and what we usually measure?
00:34 Jordan Lee: yeah sure, um so usually we do a 3-week pilot: week one is data and golden prompt collection, week two is perf and correctness runs, week three is regression and handoffs. We measure correctness via a golden set and an automated scorer, plus manual spot checks for hallucinations and format compliance.
00:52 Marcus Chen: two quick constraints: one, we need SOC2-compliant logs and KMS integration for keys; two, can you support a VPC deployment or private tenancy?
01:04 Priya Kapoor: yes on both, for POC we can do a private deployment into a customer VPC or dedicated capacity depending on what you prefer, and we have KMS integrations. We'll share our security playbook after the call.
01:16 Lydia Park: for workload sizing, our inference mix is about 70% short prompts (<256 tokens) and 30% long document parsing (~2k tokens) — the long ones are where hallucinations hurt the most. Our expected concurrency for POC is 50 concurrent users, approx 120 qps overall.
01:36 Jordan Lee: okay good to know; for perf runs we typically simulate the concurrency profile and run steady-state tests plus spike/burst tests. For KV/prefix caching — we need representative prefixes to measure cache hit rate, because that changes cost and latency significantly.
01:50 Dr. Elena Ruiz: for quality eval plan, we want a few things: golden prompts for top 20 intents, regression tests for critical flows, hallucination detection rules (medical facts must match source), and format checks for structured outputs (CSV/JSON schema). We also want an explicit scoring rubric.
02:08 Samir Patel: perfect that's exactly alignable. Proposed scoring approach: each golden prompt gets an automatic score 0-1 for schema match, 0-1 for factual correctness (automated heuristics plus reference check), and 0-1 for hallucination risk (overlap with source docs). We weight schema highly for billing flows. If aggregate score across sample set >= 0.9 we mark as pass for that flow.
02:30 Marcus Chen: can you be explicit about what the automated heuristics for factual correctness look like? It's critical for us to trust the automation.
02:38 Jordan Lee: yep, so heuristics include entity matching against canonical patient data, citation matching for referenced guidelines, and a semantic similarity check to the source doc. For tricky clinical claims we flag for manual review. We'll provide the heuristics in the eval template and note the caveats.
02:54 Lydia Park: what about hallucination classification? We need a conservative approach — false negatives are dangerous.
03:00 Samir Patel: agreed. For hallucination detection we'll use a combination: answer-to-source alignment (does the assertion appear in the source), a contradiction detector, and a model-based hallucination scorer. We tune thresholds conservatively for clinical POCs and also include a manual spot-check sample (5% of outputs) for validation.
03:20 Dr. Elena Ruiz: ok that sounds reasonable. For the golden prompts, we can provide 100 examples across intents but we expect you to sample a 20-example per-intent golden set for automated runs.
03:32 Jordan Lee: that works. We'll need also negative cases — prompts that should produce NO answer or "refer to specialist" — to ensure the model abstains rather than hallucinate.
03:42 Samir Patel: good point. We'll include abstention/regression tests. On benchmarks we'll measure P95 latency, p99 tail, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens for the real load. For the POC we'll run both hosted Redwood and dedicated instance configs so you can compare.
03:58 Marcus Chen: what's the typical timeline to get the dedicated environment spun up?
04:02 Priya Kapoor: for dedicated we can provision reserved capacity in 1-2 weeks for POC, VPC/private installs may take longer depending on approvals — usually 2-4 weeks. For the initial perf runs we can start on hosted with data obfuscation while infra is provisioned.
04:18 Lydia Park: regarding data handling, can you support in-flight encryption and audit logs per request?
04:23 Samir Patel: yes, we have request-level audit logs, and you can bring your own key via KMS for encryption at rest. We'll include the security page.
04:32 Dr. Elena Ruiz: great. For scoring thresholds you mentioned 0.9 pass. If we have mixed results across intents, what's the remediation path?
04:40 Jordan Lee: we typically run targeted tuning: prompt engineering, temperature/penalty adjustments, and if needed we recommend quantized model variants or a smaller specialized model for structured extraction. We'll run a second regression after changes.
04:54 Marcus Chen: do you do model rollout policies in POC? Like can we try different variants and fallback?
04:59 Samir Patel: yes, Redwood supports route-based policies and automatic fallback to a cheaper variant on overload. For POC we'll test one primary model and one fallback model to validate behavior.
05:10 Lydia Park: what about hallucination metrics over time? We want a trend chart, not just a single pass/fail.
05:15 Priya Kapoor: we can provide dashboards in Redwood Console showing hallucination score trends, schema compliance, and token costs over the test window. We'll include links in the final report.
05:25 Dr. Elena Ruiz: ok. Can you walk through an example golden prompt and scoring?
05:28 Jordan Lee: sure — example: prompt to extract billing codes from a discharge summary. Golden answer: JSON array of codes, reason, and confidence. Automated checks: 1) JSON schema match (0/1), 2) code validity against ICD-10 list (0/1), 3) hallucination check (does code appear in source context) (0/1). If it scores 3/3 that's 1.0. If many prompts fall below 0.9 we list failure modes and recommended changes.
06:00 Dr. Elena Ruiz: how do you handle ambiguous cases where clinician clinical language is vague? The model might produce multiple plausible interpretations.
06:09 Samir Patel: we classify those as 'ambiguous' and include an abstain or clarification template. For POC scoring we mark ambiguous cases separately and track how often abstraction/clarification templates are used.
06:20 Lydia Park: for workload sizing you asked concurrency — any suggestions on what synthetic load to run? We asked for 120 qps, 50 concurrent — is that sustained?
06:28 Jordan Lee: yes simulate steady-state 120 qps for 30 minutes then a 5-minute spike to 300 qps to observe autoscaling and tail latency. We'll also run long-sequence tests for the 2k token cases which are cost heavy.
06:44 Marcus Chen: do you record per-token cost during the run? Need to show cost projection for production.
06:50 Samir Patel: yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost breakdown and per-route cost projection. We'll include a cost delta between hosted and dedicated for the same run.
07:00 Dr. Elena Ruiz: any red flags we should know about upfront?
07:03 Jordan Lee: only that long-context extraction can be sensitive to prompt framing; we may need to try a few prompt families. Also KV cache behavior can vary; if your prefixes are highly variable cache hit rate will be low and costs remain higher.
07:18 Lydia Park: okay. For the POC acceptance criteria can we put it as: 1) average schema compliance >= 95% for billing flows, 2) hallucination rate <= 2% on critical intents, 3) P95 latency < 300ms for short prompts and <1s for long prompts on dedicated, and 4) cost per 1k tokens within X% of target (we'll define)?
07:41 Samir Patel: that looks good; we can draft that formally in the POC doc. For hallucination threshold we'll discuss how to compute (false positive vs false negative) and agree the exact metric.
07:52 Dr. Elena Ruiz: timeline-wise, if we share sample data by 2025-04-08 can we start automated runs the week of 2025-04-14?
07:59 Priya Kapoor: yes that's feasible. Infra deep-dive would be week of 2025-04-14 and perf runs during 2025-04-15 to 04-22. Final report by 2025-04-25.
08:12 Marcus Chen: who will own the final decision sign-off? For us it will be Dr. Ruiz and CTO; for Redwood who signs off?
08:19 Samir Patel: typically AE and SE (me and Jordan) confirm POC completion and sign off, and we'll present the final runbook.
08:26 Dr. Elena Ruiz: ok. A couple of small clarifying Qs: do you store sample data? We prefer you not to persist any PII.
08:32 Samir Patel: we recommend data obfuscation or tokenization for hosted runs; for dedicated/VPC we can avoid any retention by configuration and you can bring your own KMS. We'll capture that in security doc.
08:44 Lydia Park: last question — how will you score hallucination that is plausible but incorrect? e.g., citing a wrong drug dose.
08:50 Jordan Lee: those are flagged both as factual mismatch and high hallucination score; we show them in the manual review queue with source snippets for triage.
08:58 Dr. Elena Ruiz: thanks, that helps.
09:01 Samir Patel: great, quick recap of next steps: Samir to share benchmark spreadsheet + golden prompt template by 2025-04-06; MedSys to share 2 weeks sample queries + 100 golden examples by 2025-04-08; Jordan to prepare perf config; schedule infra call week of 2025-04-14. Any objections?
09:20 Marcus Chen: none.
09:22 Dr. Elena Ruiz: sounds good.
09:24 Priya Kapoor: we'll send calendar invites and the security pack after the call.
09:28 Samir Patel: awesome thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and Slack.
09:32 (call ends)
